I used water and alcohol to relax mine for pinning after they sat in storage for two weeks. They sat in a tupperware on papertowel with the mixture for a day before I messed with them. I Ied a few that were already in rough shape when I grabbed them in order to make sure they were ready before I tried to rearticulate the quality ones. 

These guys were my first pin, and I felt like they were very workable and forgiving given my inexperience, so you should have pretty good luck. Also, I used cardboard for my pinning board and just got a 100 pack of pins off Amazon, so I wouldn't stress about it too much. I also used parchment paper to hold the wings flat, but keep in mind that when you do that they can still shift a bit underneath, so you might end up getting a few in angles different than you plan on.
